concepts.name: NDMA: Statutory Basis and Constitutional Anchoring
key_dimensions: Established under Disaster Management Act, 2005 — not a constitutional body
Entry 23 (State List) vs. Centre's role — how DM Act overrides via Concurrent List Entry 29
NDMA as successor to High Powered Committee (HPC) and National Crisis Management Committee (NCMC)
Distinction: NDMA (statutory) vs. NCMC (executive/non-statutory) — UPSC trap on overlap

concepts.name: Composition and Chairpersonship of NDMA
key_dimensions: PM as ex-officio Chairperson — unique feature among statutory bodies
Maximum 9 members including Vice-Chairperson appointed by PM
Comparison trap: NDMA (PM heads) vs. SDMA (CM heads) vs. DDMA (District Collector/DM heads)
Vice-Chairperson holds Cabinet Minister rank — significance for coordination

concepts.name: NDMA's Core Mandate: The 4R Framework
key_dimensions: Prevention, Mitigation, Preparedness, Response, Recovery, Reconstruction — Sendai alignment
Shift from reactive (relief-centric) to proactive (risk reduction) paradigm post-2005
NDMA's role confined to policy/guidelines — implementation delegated to NDRF and State agencies
UPSC trap: NDMA does not directly conduct rescue operations — NDRF does

concepts.name: National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP): Hierarchy and Revision
key_dimensions: First NDMP released in 2016, revised in 2019 — aligned with Sendai Framework 2015–2030
NDMP is prepared by NDMA and approved by the Central Government
Five thematic areas: Understanding Risk, Inter-Agency Coordination, Investing in DRR, Preparedness, Capacity Development
Distinction: NDMP (national level) vs. State DM Plans vs. District DM Plans — legal obligation for each

concepts.name: National Disaster Response Force (NDRF): Control and Deployment
key_dimensions: NDRF under NDMA's overall supervision but day-to-day control with Director General of NDRF
Constituted under Section 44-45 of DM Act — 16 battalions drawn from CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP, SSB
UPSC trap: NDRF is not under MHA directly — it operates under NDMA's guidance
Proactive deployment vs. reactive deployment — NDMA can pre-position NDRF before disaster strikes

concepts.name: NDMA Guidelines vs. Directions: Legal Force and Compliance
key_dimensions: Section 6: NDMA lays down policies, plans, guidelines — these are binding on Ministries/Departments
UPSC trap: Guidelines ≠ mere advisories — Ministries must integrate them into their plans (Section 37)
NDMA can seek compliance reports from Ministries — quasi-regulatory power
Distinction between NDMA guidelines (policy) and NDRF SOPs (operational protocols)

concepts.name: Sendai Framework 2015–2030 and NDMA's Alignment
key_dimensions: Four priorities: Understanding risk, Governance, Investing in DRR, Enhancing response
Seven global targets — India's voluntary commitments and NDMA's role in tracking
Sendai replaces Hyogo Framework for Action (HFA) 2005–2015 — shift from managing disasters to managing risks
UPSC trap: Sendai is a non-binding framework — India's implementation is through DM Act and NDMP, not Sendai directly

concepts.name: National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) and National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF)
key_dimensions: NDRF under Section 46 — managed by Central Government, not NDMA directly (UPSC trap)
NDMF under Section 47 — for mitigation projects, distinct from NDRF (relief) and SDRF
State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) — Centre contributes 75% (90% for NE/hilly states)
CALAMITY RELIEF FUND (CRF) subsumed into SDRF post-2005 — historical evolution question

concepts.name: Role of NDMA in Minimum Standards of Relief
key_dimensions: Section 12: NDMA recommends minimum standards of relief — food, water, sanitation, medical care
These standards are binding on State Governments implementing relief operations
Sphere Project international standards vs. NDMA's domestic minimum standards — comparison angle
UPSC trap: NDMA recommends, but State Governments and SDMAs implement relief — division of roles

concepts.name: NDMA and Early Warning Systems: Mandate and Institutional Gaps
key_dimensions: NDMA mandates early warning dissemination but IMD, INCOIS, GSI are technical agencies (not under NDMA)
Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) — NDMA's push for standardized multi-hazard alerts
Last-mile connectivity challenge — Cell Broadcasting System and Integrated Alert System
UPSC trap: NDMA coordinates early warning but does not generate forecasts — overlap with IMD/INCOIS

concepts.name: District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA): Composition and Powers
key_dimensions: District Collector/DM as Chairperson — elected representative (Zila Panchayat President) as Co-Chairperson
UPSC trap: In areas with Municipal Corporation, Mayor may be Co-Chairperson — urban context
DDMA is the pivotal implementation authority — first responder coordination at ground level
DDMA prepares District DM Plan, which must be consistent with State and National plans

concepts.name: NDMA's Hazard-Specific Guidelines: Scope and Limitations
key_dimensions: NDMA has issued guidelines for earthquakes, floods, cyclones, landslides, chemical disasters, biological disasters, nuclear/radiological disasters
UPSC trap: NDMA guidelines exist for biological disasters — relevant post-COVID for Prelims/Mains
Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear (CBRN) disasters — overlap with MHA and DRDO mandates
Limitation: Guidelines are policy documents — no penal provision for non-compliance by states

concepts.name: National Executive Committee (NEC): Role and Relationship with NDMA
key_dimensions: NEC headed by Union Home Secretary — coordinates implementation of NDMA policies

NEC members: Secretaries of Agriculture, Atomic Energy, Defence, Drinking Water, Environment, Finance, Health, Power, Rural Development, Science & Technology, Space, Telecom, Water Resources, and Chief of Integrated Defence Staff
UPSC trap: NDMA makes policy; NEC executes — NEC is the operational arm at Central Government level
NEC prepares National Plan and submits to NDMA for approval — direction of approval flow

concepts.name: Disaster Classification: Natural vs. Man-made and NDMA's Ambit
key_dimensions: DM Act does not define 'disaster' exhaustively — NDMA's mandate covers both natural and man-made
UPSC trap: Industrial accidents (Bhopal-type) fall under Environment Protection Act AND DM Act — dual jurisdiction
COVID-19 declared a 'notified disaster' under DM Act — expanding scope of NDMA powers
Exclusion: Disasters arising from armed conflict — outside NDMA purview (handled under Armed Forces Acts)

concepts.name: NDMA's Role in Urban Disaster Risk Reduction
key_dimensions: Urban Flood guidelines — 2010 NDMA guidelines specifically for urban flooding
Integration with Smart Cities Mission and AMRUT — NDMA's advisory role in urban planning
UPSC trap: Building byelaws and land-use planning remain with State/ULB — NDMA cannot enforce directly
National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project (NCRMP) — World Bank funded, NDMA coordinates

concepts.name: PM-10 Point Agenda and NDMA's Thematic Priorities
key_dimensions: PM Modi's 10-point agenda at 2016 Asian Ministerial Conference — local governance, risk-sensitive investment, social protection, ecosystem services
Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) — India's initiative, NDMA's international role
UPSC trap: CDRI is separate from NDMA — PM-level initiative, not under DM Act
International Solar Alliance + CDRI — India's dual multilateral DRR leadership post-2015

concepts.name: Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Mainstreaming Across Ministries
key_dimensions: Section 37 of DM Act: Every Ministry must prepare DM plan consistent with NDMP
DRR integration into Five-Year Plans — now reflected in outcome budgets of line Ministries
UPSC trap: Responsibility for DRR mainstreaming is on each Ministry, not NDMA alone — NDMA only guides
School Safety Programme and Hospital Safety — NDMA-led sectoral initiatives under mainstreaming

concepts.name: NDMA vs. SDMA vs. NCMC: Jurisdictional Overlaps and Coordination Failures
key_dimensions: NCMC (Cabinet Secretary heads) — for major disasters requiring inter-ministerial coordination, parallel to NDMA
UPSC trap: NCMC is executive, not statutory — can be convened without NDMA involvement
SDMA mirrors NDMA at state level but CM heads it — SDMA cannot override NDMA guidelines
Inter-agency coordination failure case: Kedarnath 2013 — exposed gaps between NDMA, SDMA, and NDRF deployment

concepts.name: Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM) and NDMA Guidelines
key_dimensions: NDMA guidelines emphasize Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies as first responders
Aapda Mitra Scheme — training community volunteers, linked to NDMA's capacity-building mandate
UPSC trap: Aapda Mitra is operationalized by NDMA but funded under SDRF norms — finance-implementation split
Gendered approach to DRR — NDMA guidelines on inclusion of women in disaster preparedness committees

concepts.name: Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA) and NDMA's Role in Recovery Planning
key_dimensions: PDNA methodology — joint World Bank-UN framework adopted by India for structured recovery
NDMA coordinates PDNA but financial releases happen through Finance Ministry/NDRF — UPSC trap on who controls funds
Build Back Better principle — NDMA guidelines on ensuring reconstructed infrastructure is disaster-resilient
Distinction: Immediate relief (SDRF), medium-term recovery (NDRF), long-term reconstruction (Planning/Line Ministries)
